idea:
Artificial intelligence is running out of compute. And data centers are running out of electricity and land.

The demand for data centers is insatiable. But new data centers can take years for approval and enough megawatts, and still could get killed by local government intervention.

While communities increasingly oppose the land, the water is open.

It sounds crazy, but we think part of the answer may be to move compute offshore.

The ocean is 70% of the Earth's surface area, has abundant sunlight, no permitting process, and is an enormous natural heat sink that is already getting hit by the sun all day anyway. Think of them as compute flotillas: many standardized, modular vessels operating together as one global cloud.

We want to fund founders who are bringing the world's compute to the oceans.

brand.name: AEGIR
brand.tagline: Sovereign compute, cooled by the deep.
brand.audience: Deep-tech founders and sovereign investors bypassing land-grid constraints.
brand.visualConcept: A brutalist maritime-telemetry interface. Dark abyssal slate contrasted with high-visibility international orange and glowing sonar green, featuring wireframe bathymetric ocean floor maps.
brand.layout: A single-scroll command center dashboard. Features a massive hero statement, a real-time interactive 3D globe showing oceanic thermal currents, and a terminal-style application portal.
creativeNotes: Replace standard illustrations with interactive, low-poly 3D models of modular server-barges floating on a dark, reflective WebGL ocean.
Use SVG bathymetric contour lines as structural grid dividers that warp dynamically as the user scrolls.
Incorporate a persistent 'Telemetry Feed' ticker at the top of the page displaying simulated wave heights, cooling efficiency, and latency metrics.
